title: Design blocked GF(p) echelon / RREF kernel (026fc832 Phase 6)
description:
Phase 6 design task under epic `026fc832`. Designs (NOT implements) a blocked GF(p) echelon / RREF kernel that derives from the panelized PLE (sibling task) plus blocked triangular solve.

Parent epic: `026fc832`. Predecessor: the panelized PLE design (sibling task in the same wave).

## Background

A8 rows 18-29 (echelon GF(7/251/65521) at all n/regimes), rows 72-73 (GF(31) echelon), and rows 30-33 (echelon GF(2^31-1)). The current `FieldMatrix::rref` uses the (bd9c6e13-fixed) scalar PLE then triangular-solves. Blocking the second pass to use the panelized PLE's L1 factor + GEMM-based triangular-solve is expected to inherit the fgemm speedup and close most echelon FAIL cells.

The design must address:
- How the blocked echelon derives from the panelized PLE output (use L1/U1 factors directly).
- Blocked back-substitution using a panel GEMM call (call into the existing `fp_small_try_gemm_classical` from `gf2-kernels-simd`).
- Whether GF(2^31-1) Mersenne31 cells require a separate Mersenne31-specialised path or can share the small-prime infrastructure.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] A design document attached via `jit doc add` describing the blocked echelon algorithm, dependency on the panelized PLE (sibling design), and the back-sub blocking.
- [hard] Test surface specified (proptest correctness vs scalar reference; rank-deficient regimes).
- [hard] Benchmark cells listed (matching A8 rows 18-33, 72-73).
- [hard] The design names the SSOT helpers it reuses (panelized PLE, `fp_small_try_gemm_classical`).
- [hard] No production code — design only.
- [hard] The design lists the single implementation child needed.

## Out of scope

- Implementation.
- PLE, invert, solve designs — siblings.
- Mersenne31 dense-LA if it requires fundamentally different infrastructure (state this in the design with a rationale).
